title: Unload a carousel: crate each red block before its carrier comes back round to the loader
instruction: Load the five blocks onto the carousel at the green marker. Crate each red block before it returns to that marker; leave the blue ones riding.
context: At machine-paced stations a bench-top indexing carousel carries parts round: one tender loads each pallet at the loading station, the other takes each finished (red) part off at the unload station before its pallet comes back to the loader, which needs a free pallet. Blue parts are in process and ride on, so a returning pallet with a blue part is normal. Done by packaging and filling machine operators and tenders (O*NET 51-9111.00; 371,600 employed) and packers and packagers, hand (O*NET 53-7064.00; 645,210 employed), BLS OEWS May 2023, about 1.0 million together; tending a machine and clearing finished product before the next arrives is regular core work. Two fixed tending stations, each arm its own. Nothing is handed between arms; the new elements are a per-block deadline and per-block provenance.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; table top oak, arm bases 61 cm apart. Carousel: six square carrier plates of anodised aluminium (11 x 11 x 1.2 cm, friction 0.8) ride 2 mm above the table on a circle of radius 18 cm about (34, 0), one per 60 degrees, around a dark steel hub 10 x 10 x 3 cm. Every 5 s the machine indexes one slot clockwise seen from above (1.2 s of motion, 3.8 s standing; first index at 5 s); one lap takes 30 s. Slot 0, the loader, is at (34, +18) beside a green marker strip (12 x 1.5 cm) at (34, 26.2); slot 3, the unload slot, is at (34, -18). Supply mat: rubber, 34 x 20 x 0.4 cm, centre (34, 44), carrying five 5 cm solid acetal cubes of 176 g (1.41 g/cm3): red at (23, 37), (32, 37), (41, 37) and blue at (27.5, 49), (36.5, 49). Crate: polypropylene tray, inside 26 cm (x 17 to 43) by 36 cm (y -62 to -26), 0.5 cm floor, 0.8 cm walls, 6 cm tall above the table (5.5 cm above the floor, 5 mm over a block's top). Cameras: top, above the table; left and right wrist.
scoring: A per-step monitor follows each block. Loaded: first resting on a carrier plate (bottom within 8 mm of its top) with both grippers clear. A carrier's first return: back within 8 cm of the loader slot after being over 12 cm away. A red block is credited only if it was loaded, was off every carrier before its carrier's first return (still riding at or after it: never counts), never rested on the table or floor after loading, and now rests on the crate floor (bottom within 6 mm), inside the walls, under 1 cm/s, with both grippers at least 4 cm plus finger opening clear. A blue block is spoiled if after loading it is lifted over 3 cm off its plate, lost or crated. A block taken straight off the supply mat is never credited. 0.25: three or more blocks loaded; 0.5: one red credited; 0.75: two reds credited; 1.0: all five loaded, all three reds credited, both blues still riding, held 1 s. A spoiled blue caps the score at 0.5. Check: ruler and stopwatch against the carousel clock.
reset_notes: Carrier plates in their six slots with the loader slot at the green marker, carousel stopped at index 0 until 5 s; blocks on the supply mat at the marked spots; crate empty at its marks.
fidelity: Approximate. Carriers follow the indexing path exactly (driven bodies, like a servo carousel; no track, drive or inertia; they translate without turning). Blocks are 50 mm acetal cubes for small parts; red/blue colour marks finished/in-process. Provenance, return and credit are tracked by code from object poses. The other arm is the loader. A red set down outside the crate is lost; a disturbed blue is spoiled (scoring).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (neither arm touched a block); demo: 1.0 (left arm loaded the five blocks, right arm crated each red block before its carrier returned)
